Definition.text:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Fix a complex affine algebraic group $G$ with no nontrivial closed normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional rational module has a nonzero fixed vector; this is the reductive hypothesis. Fix a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, fix a finite-dimensional complex $\mathbb Z/2$-graded vector space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, a field parity, and an algebraic representation $\rho_i:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\Phi_i)$. Include the declared spacetime-index action in $G$ or in its specified finite-dimensional representation data. A field configuration assigns smooth component functions on $M$ to the even generators and formal odd Grassmann generators with smooth coefficient functions to the odd generators.

Fix a derivative cutoff $r\geq0$, a maximum polynomial field degree $q\geq0$, and a rational engineering weight $\Delta_i$ for each field species. A derivative $\partial_\mu$ has engineering weight one, and an $s$-jet generator is a component of $\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_s}\phi_i(x)$ for $0\leq s\leq r$. If covariant derivatives are used, their finite jet generators and $G$-action are included explicitly in the same data. Let $J_r$ be the resulting finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z/2$-graded vector space with its specified algebraic representation $\rho_r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(J_r)$. Its polynomial algebra is the supercommutative algebra $P_r=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{r,\bar 0}^{*})\otimes\Lambda(J_{r,\bar 1}^{*})$: even generators commute and odd generators anticommute. For a fixed weight $D\in\mathbb Q$, let $P_{r,q,D}$ be the complex span of monomials of total engineering weight $D$ and total polynomial degree at most $q$.

A local operator in this finite-order data is an element of $P_{r,q,D}$ evaluated at $x$ on the $r$-jet of the fields. A scalar operator invariant under the declared symmetries is an element of $V_{r,q,D}=P_{r,q,D}^{G}$. Engineering dimension means this assigned mass weight; it is not a statement about an observed quantity. In four dimensions a term with operator $\mathcal O_D$ has the convention $C\mathcal O_D/\Lambda^{D-4}$, where $\Lambda$ has mass dimension one and $C$ is dimensionless. Reality conditions, when required for a real action, are additional conjugation data on $V_{r,q,D}$.

Definition.text:
Fix a finite jet order $r$, maximum polynomial field degree $q$, engineering weight $D$, finite field-species list, coefficient field $\mathbb C$, and complex reductive affine algebraic group $G$ with the finite-dimensional rational action specified on the jet generators, including the declared spacetime-index symmetries. Let $W_D$ be the finite-dimensional space of all local polynomials of weight $D$ and degree at most $q$, before imposing $G$-invariance, and let $V_D=W_D^G$ be its invariant scalar subspace. An admitted raw relation space is a specified $G$-stable linear subspace $\widetilde R_D\leq W_D$, given by explicit linear identities among the chosen polynomials. Its invariant part is $R_D=\widetilde R_D\cap V_D$. Any action, boundary, or observable interpretation of the selected identities is extra mathematical data and must be stated with the result that verifies it.

The finite-order invariant operator-basis quotient is

$$
\mathcal Q_D:=V_D/R_D.
$$

Two invariant operators represent the same class exactly when their difference lies in $R_D$. An operator basis is any finite list of representatives in $V_D$ of a vector-space basis of $\mathcal Q_D$. The quotient records precisely the declared relation space; it does not assert that every relation relevant to an arbitrary EFT, observable, or infinite operator tower has been included.

Definition.text:
Use four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for mass-dimension counting. A **physical EFT operator contract** is a record of the following selected model data; none of the selections is inferred from an operator's name.

Here an EFT is an adopted low-energy model whose local Lagrangian is organized by specified fields, symmetries, coefficients, and a finite retained order; this definition implies no ultraviolet completion or physical realization. First choose a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, specify a finite-dimensional complex graded space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, its bosonic or fermionic parity, its smooth field domain on $M$, any reality condition, and its assigned rational engineering weight $\Delta_i$. Even fields are smooth maps $M\to\Phi_i^{\bar 0}$; odd field components take values in a fixed Grassmann algebra with smooth coefficient functions. A spurion is a fixed, non-dynamical parameter assigned a representation and engineering weight, used to record a declared symmetry-breaking insertion. The proper orthochronous Lorentz group is $SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\ \det L=1,\ L^0{}_0\ge1\}$; specify its finite-dimensional action on all spacetime indices and require each Lagrangian density to be a Lorentz scalar. State the full gauge and flavor actions on every field, index, and spurion. A flavor symmetry that is absent is recorded as trivial; an approximate or explicitly broken symmetry requires its breaking spurions and weights to be listed.

For a non-Abelian gauge sector, specify the compact real gauge group with its actual global form, smooth right principal bundle, admitted bundle sectors, unitary representations, and a smooth principal connection. The connection is a Lie-algebra-valued one-form reproducing fundamental vertical vectors and transforming by the adjoint action; its local curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, and the covariant derivative in a representation $\rho$ is $D_\mu\psi=\partial_\mu\psi+\rho_*(A_\mu)\psi$. The field and connection data must include their regularity and spacetime and internal index representations. These formulas use the right-principal-bundle convention fixed by the supplied gauge-geometry definitions.

The local operator algebra uses a separate finite-dimensional rational representation of a complex reductive affine algebraic group $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ on the finite jet generators. A contract must supply the maps and representations relating $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ to the selected compact gauge group and flavor group. It must either verify, on each retained finite jet space, that the algebraic invariant subspace is exactly the intended physical invariant space, or label the quotient as a formal algebraic selection only. Compactness of a real gauge group alone does not identify its invariant polynomials with those of an algebraic complexification.

Choose nonnegative integer cutoffs $r$ and $q$, a coefficient field (here $\mathbb C$) and its conjugation data, and a finite rational maximum engineering dimension $D_{\max}$. With derivatives assigned weight one, the local field-jet definition supplies the supercommutative polynomial module $P_r=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{r,\bar 0}^*)\otimes\Lambda(J_{r,\bar 1}^*)$ and its fixed-weight subspaces. For each weight $D$, let $W_D$ be the finite raw polynomial space, $V_D=W_D^{G_{\mathrm{alg}}}$ its invariant scalar subspace, and $\widetilde R_D$ the explicitly declared $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$-stable linear relation subspace. The selected operator quotient is $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/(\widetilde R_D\cap V_D)$: it identifies exactly the declared relations and makes no completeness claim about all EFT redundancies. For each retained $D$, choose a vector-space basis of $\mathcal Q_D$ and one representative $\mathcal O_\alpha\in V_D$ of each basis class; write $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}$ for the resulting finite set of representative labels and $\Delta_\alpha$ for the weight of $\mathcal O_\alpha$. The finite jet, field-degree, and dimension cutoffs give a finite-dimensional retained space, and the fixed-cutoff monomial set gives finitely many retained weights and representatives.

For each $\widetilde R_D$, record each generator as a polynomial or Fierz identity, a total divergence under compact-support or stated boundary conditions, or a leading-equation or field-redefinition relation tied to an explicit base action and retained order. An equation-of-motion entry records its variational derivative and field multiplier; a field-redefinition entry records the local map, its inverse through the retained order, and all induced higher-order terms. The quotient is a definition of the declared relation space; its existence alone does not establish action, off-shell Green-function, quantum-measure, or scattering equivalence.

Choose the canonical-dimension power-counting scheme, coefficient truncation, and a nonnegative integer loop order $L_{\max}$. The formal loop label $\zeta$ is dimensionless bookkeeping and is not a convergence claim. If $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ is the coefficient-suppression scale, the retained local Lagrangian has the convention

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}\\\Delta_\alpha\le D_{\max}}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L_{\max}}\zeta^\ell C_{\alpha,\ell}(\mu_W)\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{\Delta_\alpha-4}},$$

where each $\mathcal O_\alpha$ has engineering weight $\Delta_\alpha$, each $C_{\alpha,\ell}$ is dimensionless in the stated natural units, and the chosen reality conditions make $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}$ real. This is canonical-dimension counting for the selected linear EFT; HEFT chiral counting and multi-scale SCET counting are different schemes and are not implied. A truncation order is not a numerical error bound, a coefficient prediction, or a derived renormalization-group flow.

If the same application also uses a finite-regulator data record, retain its graph variables, measure, Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, heavy mass $M$, external-energy bound $E$, and regulator cutoff $\Lambda$ with their supplied meanings. The operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda$, $M$, $E$, and $\mu_W$ are distinct parameters unless an additional model input identifies them. A map from finite-graph variables to the continuum finite-jet operator data is also additional input; the finite-regulator definition supplies no such map or continuum limit.

Postulate.text:
Adopt four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for engineering dimensions, so $\partial_\mu$ has mass dimension one, a scalar field has dimension one, a spinor field has dimension $3/2$, and a gauge field strength has dimension two.

The gauge group is the direct product $G_{\mathrm{SM}}=SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$, with this global form and not a quotient by a subgroup of its center. Write an element of $U(1)_Y$ as $z\in U(1)$ and normalize its integer charge as $y=6Y$, so its representation acts by $z^y$. The three-family matter fields and scalar are smooth fields in the representations
$$q_L:(3,2)_1,\qquad u_R:(3,1)_4,\qquad d_R:(3,1)_{-2},\qquad \ell_L:(1,2)_{-3},\qquad e_R:(1,1)_{-6},\qquad H:(1,2)_3.$$
There are no right-handed neutrino fields. Fermion components are Grassmann odd; $H$ is a Grassmann-even complex doublet. The global charges are $B(q_L)=B(u_R)=B(d_R)=1/3$, $L(\ell_L)=L(e_R)=1$, and zero for $H$ and the gauge fields; the corresponding $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_L$ transformations multiply each field by the phase determined by its charge. Impose these as exact selection rules on the retained formal local interactions; no anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. There is no flavor symmetry beyond the displayed gauge action: Yukawa and Wilson coefficients may carry unrestricted three-family indices subject to the stated reality and Hermitian-conjugation conditions.

Choose a reference symmetry-breaking radius $v>0$ of mass dimension one. If it is interpreted as a vacuum radius, the supplied scalar-potential coefficients are assumed to make $H^\dagger H=v^2/2$ a local minimum; this postulate does not derive that parameter constraint. Define $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$, where $\sigma^2$ is the second Pauli matrix.

Choose the trivial smooth right principal bundle $P=M\times G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ and only this bundle sector. A connection is a smooth right-principal connection with the convention $\omega(Z_P)=Z$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$. In a local section, a field in representation $\rho$ has covariant derivative $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+\rho_*(A_\mu)$, and the gauge curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$ with the graded-bracket convention of the supplied gauge-geometry data. The ordinary component hypercharges are $Y=y/6$; in particular $Y(H)=1/2$. The formal local interaction set imposes the exact $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_L$ selection rules stated above; no anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. Yukawa matrices are otherwise arbitrary.

The adopted object is a formal local Lagrangian density made from finitely many fields, covariant derivatives, and field strengths at one spacetime point, contracted to Lorentz scalars and invariant under the stated gauge and global actions. The renormalizable part has the gauge kinetic terms $-\tfrac14G^A_{\mu\nu}G^{A\mu\nu}-\tfrac14W^I_{\mu\nu}W^{I\mu\nu}-\tfrac14B_{\mu\nu}B^{\mu\nu}$, fermion kinetic terms $i\sum_\psi\bar\psi\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi$, Higgs kinetic term $-(D_\mu H)^\dagger D^\mu H$, the real gauge-invariant Higgs potential
$$V_4(H)=V_0-\mu_H^2H^\dagger H+\lambda(H^\dagger H)^2,\qquad V_0,\mu_H^2,\lambda\in\mathbb R,$$
and Yukawa terms
$$-\left(\bar q_LY_dHd_R+\bar q_LY_u\widetilde H u_R+\bar\ell_LY_eHe_R+\mathrm{h.c.}\right),$$
where each $Y_f$ is a complex $3\times3$ family matrix and h.c. is the Hermitian conjugate. Set the gauge theta terms to zero in this selected model. Add finite sets $I_d$ of local gauge-invariant, $B$- and $L$-neutral polynomial operators $\mathcal O_{d,i}$ at each retained dimension $d\leq6$. Retain derivative-jet order at most two, maximum polynomial field degree six, and loop order zero. Use $C_{d,i}\mathcal O_{d,i}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{d-4}$, where $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ has mass dimension one and each $C_{d,i}$ is dimensionless. The dimension-five set is empty under the adopted exact lepton-number symmetry. The dimension-six set is fixed by the separate Warsaw coefficient contract. Wilson coefficients are supplied parameters, not calculated or fitted here.

This is an operator-level model on smooth fields and compactly supported variations; total divergences are therefore zero in the associated action comparison. Its low-energy use is restricted to external momenta small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, with the finite dimension-six truncation understood formally and without a numerical remainder bound. No regulator or functional measure is adopted, and no finite graph cutoff is identified with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$. The postulate asserts no path integral, continuum limit, ultraviolet completion, or empirical realization.

Postulate.text:
Use the same four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, direct-product global gauge group, gauge connection, fermion representations, family content, and the preceding model's exact baryon- and lepton-number selection rules on formal local interactions. No anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. In particular, the hypercharge-one-half Higgs doublet of that model is replaced in this realization by three angular Goldstone coordinates and a real scalar singlet; this is a distinct adopted model interface, not a deduction that the two models have identical field spaces.

Let $J=(-v,\infty)$, where $v>0$ is the mass-one reference radius from the preceding model. A scalar field is a smooth map $h:M\to J$ and is invariant under the electroweak gauge group. The Goldstone field is a smooth map $U:M\to SU(2)$, with $SU(2)$ represented by its defining $2\times2$ unitary matrices of determinant one. For an electroweak transformation $g_L(x)\in SU(2)_L$ and $z(x)\in U(1)_Y$, set
$$g_R(z)=\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3}),\qquad U(x)\longmapsto g_L(x)U(x)g_R(z(x))^{-1},\qquad h(x)\longmapsto h(x).$$
Thus the left factor is the linearly represented $SU(2)_L$ gauge action, the right factor is the embedded hypercharge action, and $h$ is a gauge singlet. With $T_a=\sigma_a/2$ for the Pauli matrices, the exponential chart
$$U(\pi)=\exp\!\left(\frac{2i\pi^aT_a}{v}\right),\qquad \pi\in\mathbb R^3,\quad \|\pi\|<\pi v,$$
is a smooth coordinate chart near the identity; $U$ itself is the globally valued group field and is not identified with one global exponential-coordinate chart.

Write $W_\mu=W_\mu^aT_a$ and use the local covariant derivative
$$D_\mu U=\partial_\mu U+i g W_\mu U-i g' B_\mu U T_3,$$
with dimensionless gauge couplings $g,g'$ and the same right-principal connection convention as the shared gauge data. The adopted two-derivative scalar density is
$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{(2)}=-\frac12K(h)\,\partial_\mu h\,\partial^\mu h-\frac{v^2}{4}F_C(h)\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((D_\mu U)^\dagger D^\mu U\right)-V(h),$$
where $K$ and $F_C$ are supplied smooth real dimensionless functions on $J$, $K(h)>0$ and $F_C(h)>0$ on the field range used, $K(0)=F_C(0)=1$, and $V$ is a supplied real smooth potential of mass dimension four with $V'(0)=0$. Higher local interactions may use smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$, the same gauge and matter fields, covariant derivatives, and curvature tensors, with B and L conserved. This statement adopts no finite derivative or chiral truncation; the separate power-counting definition specifies those cutoffs.

The independent HEFT cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}>0$, the radius $v$, the SMEFT coefficient scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, and any finite-regulator cutoff are separate data; no equality or hierarchy among them is imposed here. The model is used only for external energies below its supplied range of validity. It adopts no functional measure or regulator and implies no path integral, ultraviolet completion, infinite-volume limit, or empirical realization.

Definition.text:
Use the HEFT fields $U$, $h$, gauge curvatures, fermions and arbitrary smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$ from the preceding HEFT model. The canonical engineering dimension $\Delta$ is the mass weight of the local polynomial in fields and derivatives; it is the weight supplied by the finite-jet operator definition. The **chiral/loop count** is separate data and is not inferred from $\Delta$.

Adopt the electroweak chiral loop convention of Buchalla, Catà and Krause. A connected finite diagram has loop number $L\in\mathbb N_0$. Its external lines are counted by $F_L$ left-handed fermions, $F_R$ right-handed fermions, $V$ gauge bosons, $B$ Goldstone bosons, and $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ scalar singlets. In the leading Lagrangian, let $\nu_k$ count Yukawa vertices with $k$ Goldstone legs, $m_l$ gauge-Goldstone vertices with $l$ Goldstone legs, $r_s$ two-gauge-boson vertices with $s$ Goldstone legs, $x$ quartic gauge vertices, $u$ triple-gauge vertices, $z_L,z_R$ left- and right-handed fermion-gauge vertices, $\tau_{tb}$ Yukawa vertices with $t$ Goldstone legs and $b$ scalar legs, and $\omega_q$ scalar-potential vertices with $q$ scalar legs. Set
$$\nu=\sum_k\nu_k+\sum_{t,b}\tau_{tb},\qquad m=\sum_lm_l,\qquad r=\sum_sr_s,\qquad z=z_L+z_R,\qquad \omega=\sum_q\omega_q.$$
For these counts the source chiral degree of the external-momentum factor is
$$d_\chi=2L+2-\frac{F_L+F_R}{2}-V-\nu-m-2r-2x-u-z-2\omega.$$
The factors $(\varphi/v)^B$ and $(h/v)^{H_{\mathrm{ext}}}$ contain any number of Goldstone and singlet fields and do not increase $d_\chi$. Vertices $\varphi^{2j}h^a$ from the leading two-derivative scalar sector likewise carry no additional term in this degree formula. Here $\varphi$ denotes the local Goldstone coordinates defined by $U=\exp(2i\varphi^aT_a/v)$ in its stated coordinate chart. The chiral cutoff and loop cutoff are supplied independently; this contract retains the leading order and the one-loop next-to-leading counterterm classes with $L\leq1$ and $d_\chi\geq0$.

The finite next-to-leading structural classes are $UhD^4$, $X^2Uh$, $XUhD^2$, $\psi^2UhD$, $\psi^2UhD^2$, and $\psi^4Uh$, where $U h$ means any number of $U,U^\dagger,h$ factors, $X_{\mu\nu}$ is a gauge curvature, $D$ is a covariant derivative, and $\psi$ is a fermion. Each class may carry a separate smooth function of $h/v$; the count does not truncate its Taylor series in $h$. No class list or operator-level coefficient relation from a finite canonical-dimension SMEFT basis is identified with this full HEFT list.

The scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}>0$ controlling the derivative expansion and the symmetry-breaking scale $v>0$ are separate supplied mass scales. A condition such as external momentum small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}$ is an applicability assumption only. Chiral order and loop order are formal organizing labels, not convergence claims or numerical bounds on omitted terms.

Definition.text:
Fix the field data and Minkowski convention from the earlier finite-jet definition and a truncation order $N\geq0$. A regulated perturbative generating datum consists, for each regulator label $\rho$, of a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z/2$-graded complex space $X_\rho$ of field-mode coordinates, a specified integration functional $d\mu_\rho$ on its even/odd coordinates, a local action $S_{\rho,\epsilon}:X_\rho\to\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^{N+1})$, and a generating functional

$$
Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[J]=\int_{X_\rho}\exp\!\bigl(iS_{\rho,\epsilon}(\varphi)+i\langle J,\varphi\rangle\bigr)\,d\mu_\rho(\varphi),\qquad Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[0]\text{ is a unit},
$$

where $J\in X_\rho^*$ is a linear source and the integral is either an actual convergent finite-dimensional integral or a specified formal perturbative integral. “A unit” means that the constant coefficient of $Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[0]$ is nonzero, so the normalized functional $Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[J]/Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[0]$ is defined in the truncated ring. An admissible field-coordinate change is a local, parity-preserving formal map $F_{\rho,\epsilon}:X_\rho\to X_\rho$ with $F_{\rho,0}=\operatorname{id}$ and an inverse modulo $\epsilon^{N+1}$; local means each output field at $x$ depends on a finite jet at $x$. Its regulated Jacobian factor $\mathcal J_{F,\rho}$ is the factor specified by the exact change-of-variables identity

$$
\int h(\varphi)\,d\mu_\rho(\varphi)=\int h(F_{\rho,\epsilon}(\psi))\,\mathcal J_{F,\rho}(\psi)\,d\mu_\rho(\psi)
$$

for every admissible integrand $h$; no assertion that this factor is $1$ is part of the definition. In the transformed coordinates the source is $J\cdot F_{\rho,\epsilon}(\psi)$, so the field insertion remains the same named original coordinate.

An LSZ amplitude datum is an additional limit of connected momentum-space Green functions as regulators are removed, when that limit exists. The connected $n$-point function is $i^{-n}$ times the $n$th source derivative of $\log(Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[J]/Z_{\rho,\epsilon}[0])$ at $J=0$, Fourier transformed with convention $\widetilde f(p)=\int e^{ip\cdot x}f(x)\,d^4x$; the overall momentum-conservation delta function is removed. For each external one-particle channel $a$ (with a fixed polarization component when the field has spin), the datum specifies a mass $m_a>0$ and nonzero simple-pole residue $Z_a$ at $s_a=m_a^2$, where $s_a=-\eta^{\mu\nu}p_{a,\mu}p_{a,\nu}$. Here “stable external channel” means precisely that this isolated pole exists with nonzero residue and zero width. The transformed interpolating fields must have an invertible one-particle overlap matrix; this is part of the datum. For every $n$-point function it requires pole factorization

$$
G_n(p_1,\ldots,p_n)=\left(\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{Z_{a_j}^{1/2}}{s_j-m_{a_j}^2}\right)\mathcal A_n(p_1,\ldots,p_n)+\text{terms missing at least one external pole}.
$$

The normalized LSZ amplitude is the joint residue

$$
\mathcal A_n=\left(\prod_{j=1}^n Z_{a_j}^{-1/2}\right)\lim_{s_j\to m_{a_j}^2}\left(\prod_{j=1}^n(s_j-m_{a_j}^2)\right)G_n.
$$

This definition supplies only the regulator and pole data needed for a conditional amplitude statement. It does not assert that a continuum limit, stable particles, or LSZ poles exist for a given quantum field theory.

Statement.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a complex reductive affine algebraic group, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space with an algebraic representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$, and let $N\leq V$ be a linear subspace satisfying $\rho(g)N=N$ for every $g\in G$. Define $V^G=\{v\in V:\rho(g)v=v\text{ for all }g\in G\}$, give $V/N$ the induced representation, and let $\pi:V\to V/N$ be the quotient map. Then the restriction $\pi^G:V^G\to(V/N)^G$ is surjective and has kernel $V^G\cap N$. Consequently the map

$$
V^G/(V^G\cap N)\longrightarrow(V/N)^G,\qquad v+(V^G\cap N)\longmapsto v+N
$$

is a canonical complex-linear isomorphism.

Statement.text:
Assume full AC. Use four-dimensional natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and a finite jet-polynomial field model with its declared finite rational action of a complex reductive affine algebraic group $G$. Let $W_D$ be a finite raw local-polynomial space at fixed engineering weight $D$, derivative cutoff, and field-degree cutoff; let $V_D=W_D^G$. Let $\widetilde R_D$ be the $G$-stable linear span in $W_D$ of the declared polynomial identities, admitted total-divergence densities, and leading-equation densities $F^a\mathcal E_a^{(0)}$ defined below, with $R_D=\widetilde R_D\cap V_D$. The finite-order invariant operator quotient is $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/R_D$.

Let $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $x^0=ct$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and volume measure $d^4x$. Even field components are smooth maps $M\to\Phi_a^{\bar0}$ and odd components are smooth coefficient families in a fixed Grassmann algebra valued in $\Phi_a^{\bar1}$; admitted variations and currents have compact support. Let $\mathcal I[L]=\int_M L\,d^4x$ on admitted local densities, with the boundary convention $\mathcal I(\partial_\mu J^\mu)=0$. Let $S_0[\phi]$ and each $S_j[\phi]$ be $G$-invariant local polynomial functionals of these field configurations, so their formal Taylor expansions through order $N$ are defined. Let the variational derivative $\mathcal E_a^{(0)}[\phi]$ of $S_0$ be defined by

$$
D S_0[\phi](h)=\mathcal I\!\left(\sum_a h^a\mathcal E_a^{(0)}[\phi]\right)
$$

for every admitted compactly supported parity-compatible variation $h$. A leading-equation relation is a density $F^a\mathcal E_a^{(0)}$ with local, compact-support-preserving, parity-compatible $G$-equivariant $F^a[\phi]$ for which this density lies in $W_D$; an integration-by-parts relation is a density $\partial_\mu J^\mu$ satisfying the stated boundary convention. Consider a finite formal action $S_\epsilon=S_0+\sum_{j=1}^N\epsilon^jS_j$ in the ring $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^{N+1})$, where $\epsilon$ is dimensionless and each $\epsilon^kF^a$ has the units of $\phi^a$. For every $1\leq k\leq N$, the local identity-leading change of variables $\Psi_k(\phi)=\phi-\epsilon^kF[\phi]$ is invertible as a formal map through order $N$ and satisfies

$$
S_\epsilon[\Psi_k(\phi)]=S_\epsilon[\phi]-\epsilon^k\mathcal I\!\left(F^a\mathcal E_a^{(0)}[\phi]\right)+O(\epsilon^{k+1}).
$$

Thus a coefficient $+\epsilon^k\mathcal I(F^a\mathcal E_a^{(0)})$ can be removed at order $k$ without changing lower-order coefficients, provided all induced terms through the retained order are kept. Statement.text:
Assume full AC. Let $S_\epsilon$ be a local $G$-invariant action through order $N$, with coefficients in $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^{N+1})$, where $G$ is the declared complex reductive symmetry group. Let $F_\epsilon=\operatorname{id}+O(\epsilon^k)$ be a parity-preserving local formal coordinate map with a local inverse modulo $\epsilon^{N+1}$, for some $1\leq k\leq N$, and suppose its order-$k$ difference is an admitted relation in the finite-order operator-basis quotient. For each regulator $\rho$, assume a regulated generating functional whose zero-source partition value is a unit in $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^{N+1})$ and an exact change-of-variables density factor $\mathcal J_{F,\rho}$ satisfying

$$
\int h(\varphi)\,d\mu_\rho(\varphi)=\int h(F_{\rho,\epsilon}(\psi))\,\mathcal J_{F,\rho}(\psi)\,d\mu_\rho(\psi)
$$

for every admissible integrand $h$. Define the transformed data using action $S_\epsilon\circ F_\epsilon$, this full Jacobian factor, and source $J\cdot F_\epsilon(\psi)$. Assume the common regulator limit has stable external channels $a_j$ with masses $m_{a_j}>0$, simple poles with nonzero residues $Z_{a_j}$ at $s_j=m_{a_j}^2$, where $s_j=-\eta^{\mu\nu}p_{j,\mu}p_{j,\nu}$, and connected functions that factor as

$$
G_n(p_1,\ldots,p_n)=\left(\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{Z_{a_j}^{1/2}}{s_j-m_{a_j}^2}\right)\mathcal A_n(p_1,\ldots,p_n)+\text{terms missing at least one external pole}.
$$

Here $s_j=-\eta^{\mu\nu}p_{j,\mu}p_{j,\nu}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. The normalized amplitude is the joint residue $\mathcal A_n=(\prod_j Z_{a_j}^{-1/2})\lim_{s_j\to m_{a_j}^2}(\prod_j(s_j-m_{a_j}^2))G_n$. Then the normalized source generating functionals agree through order $N$, and every normalized on-shell LSZ amplitude agrees coefficientwise modulo $\epsilon^{N+1}$. The action-level relation is a change of field coordinates with induced higher-order terms; it is not equality of the two off-shell action expressions. The conclusion does not apply after dropping the Jacobian, leaving the source untransformed, discarding induced terms, or asserting nonexistent continuum or unstable-particle LSZ limits.

Definition.text:
Use the fields, direct-product gauge group, hypercharge normalization, three-family content, exact $U(1)_B\times U(1)_L$ symmetries, natural units and coefficient scale of the preceding linearly realized model. A local operator is a finite polynomial in these fields and their covariant derivatives at one spacetime point, with all Lorentz, gauge and family indices contracted to a Lorentz and gauge scalar. Its canonical dimension assigns one to $H$ and each derivative, $3/2$ to a fermion, and two to a field strength.

The **Warsaw coefficient contract** is the finite dimension-six source list of gauge-invariant representatives $Q_i^{(6)}$ in Tables 2 and 3 of Grzadkowski, Iskrzynski, Misiak and Rosiek (2010), under their stated field, hypercharge, Lorentz, color and $SU(2)_L$ conventions, with exact baryon- and lepton-number conservation. The list consists of the source's 15 bosonic, 19 single-fermion-current and 25 four-fermion structures before family multiplicities and Hermitian conjugates; it is not a count of independent three-family complex coefficients. Include all family-index components for three generations, with the source's stated permutation, Hermiticity and conjugation rules; impose no family-universality or diagonal-flavor restriction. No right-handed neutrino field or dimension-five Weinberg operator is included.

In particular, this contract includes the source representative $Q_{H\Box}=(H^\dagger H)\Box(H^\dagger H)$, with $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ and the mostly-plus metric of the adopted model. It has canonical dimension six because each Higgs field has dimension one and $\Box$ has dimension two.

For $Q_i^{(6)}$ use the dimensionless Wilson coefficient convention
$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dim}\,6}=\frac{1}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}\sum_i C_i Q_i^{(6)},\qquad \Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0,$$
with the coefficient tensors chosen so the density is real after the required Hermitian conjugates are added. The retained operator contract has derivative-jet order at most two, maximum field degree six, canonical dimension at most six, and loop order zero. Compactly supported field variations make total divergences vanish in action-level uses.

The source's complete-basis assertion is adopted as a literature-defined coefficient list, not proved by this item. The separate finite invariant-operator quotient supplies only its declared complex-algebraic selection. In this contract that quotient is explicitly formal: no equality between its algebraic invariant space and the full physical compact-gauge invariant space, and no local proof of the EOM/IBP/Fierz classification, is claimed. The mathematical chain used to formulate that finite quotient retains its exact full Axiom of Choice premise.

Definition.text:
Let $T$ be a compact torus and $M$ a compact smooth manifold without boundary. A smooth left $T$-action is a jointly smooth map $a:T\times M\to M$ with $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(st,x)=a(s,a(t,x))$. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank complex vector bundles on $M$. For each $j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be a linear differential operator of finite order, and put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$. The sequence is a complex when $d_{j+1}d_j=0$ for every $j$. It is **elliptic** when, for every $x\in M$ and every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi\in T_x^*M$, the sequence of principal-symbol maps

$$0\longrightarrow E_x^0\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_0)(x,\xi)}E_x^1\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_1)(x,\xi)}\cdots\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_{N-1})(x,\xi)}E_x^N\longrightarrow0$$

is exact. Suppose each bundle has a smooth $T$-linearization $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$, satisfying the group-action law, and the induced section maps

$$ (U_t^j s)(x):=\rho_t^j\bigl(s(t^{-1}\cdot x)\bigr) $$

commute with $d_j$. Require the cohomology spaces $H^j(E^\bullet):=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ to be finite-dimensional. The representation ring $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of $T$. Define

$$\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j[H^j(E^\bullet)]\in R(T),\qquad \chi_{E^\bullet}(t):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}\!\left(U_t^j\bigm|_{H^j(E^\bullet)}\right).$$

For a two-term complex $0\to C^\infty(M,E^+)\xrightarrow{D^+}C^\infty(M,E^-)\to0$, this gives $[\ker D^+]-[\operatorname{coker}D^+]$. This definition concerns elliptic complexes, not transversally elliptic operators.

Definition.text:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth manifold of finite dimension $n$, with a chosen integration cycle and a smooth positive volume form $\mu$. Its parity-reversed tangent bundle $\Pi TM$ has even base coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$ and odd fiber coordinates $\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^n$, which transform as the coordinate one-forms $dx^i$. Smooth functions on $\Pi TM$ are identified with inhomogeneous complex differential forms $\mathcal A=\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)$; the parity of a form is its degree modulo two. The Berezin convention is $\int d\theta^n\cdots d\theta^1\,\theta^1\cdots\theta^n=1$. For $F\in\mathcal A$, write $F_{[n]}=f_F\mu$ for its degree-$n$ component and define the graded integral by $I_\Gamma(F):=\int_M f_F\,d\mu=\int_M F_{[n]}$, equivalently by Berezin integration over the odd fibers followed by integration over the body $M$ with the chosen orientation.

A supercharge $Q$ is a smooth odd derivation of $\mathcal A$, so for homogeneous forms $\alpha,\beta$ it satisfies $Q(\alpha\wedge\beta)=Q\alpha\wedge\beta+(-1)^{|\alpha|}\alpha\wedge Q\beta$. Its square $Q^2:=Q\circ Q$ is an even derivation. The measure and cycle are $Q$-invariant on an admissible class of integrands when $I_\Gamma(QF)=0$ for every $F$ in that class. The associated Berezinian density on $\Pi TM$ has local expression $dx^1\cdots dx^n\,d\theta^n\cdots d\theta^1$ in oriented coordinates. In that coordinate description, zero divergence means $\mathcal L_Q\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi=(\operatorname{div}_{\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi}Q)\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi=0$, together with vanishing boundary flux. Compact support in the interior or explicit decay may impose the boundary condition on a noncompact or bounded cycle.

An admissible finite-dimensional $Q$-exact deformation consists of even smooth forms $S,O\in\mathcal A$, an odd smooth form $V\in\mathcal A$, and an open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ such that $QS=QO=0$. The even form $QV$ is the $Q$-exact deformation, $S_t:=S+tQV$, and $E_t:=e^{-S_t}$, with the exponential defined by the usual pointwise exponential of its degree-zero part and the finite exterior-degree expansion of its positive-degree part. Require $(Q^2V)E_t=0$ for every $t\in J$; the stronger condition $Q^2V=0$ is sufficient. Require $O E_t$ and $O V E_t$ to be admissible integrands, with no boundary flux in $I_\Gamma(Q(O V E_t))$.

Write $(O E_t)_{[n]}=f_t\mu$. The deformation data are analytically admissible when $f_t$ is integrable for every $t\in J$, $t\mapsto f_t(x)$ is differentiable for almost every $x$, $\partial_t f_t$ is measurable, and for every compact $K\subset J$ there is a single nonnegative $g_K\in L^1(M,\mu)$ such that $|f_t(x)|\le g_K(x)$ and $|\partial_t f_t(x)|\le g_K(x)$ for every $t\in K$ outside one $\mu$-null set. The underlying manifold is finite-dimensional; its smooth-function algebra need not be finite-dimensional as a vector space.

Definition.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ on Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dt\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and spatial orientation $\epsilon_{123}=1$. Fix the global gauge group $SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$, and the trivial right principal $SU(2)$-bundle over each spatial slice. Let

$$T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a\quad(a=1,2,3),\qquad \kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY),$$

where $\sigma_a$ are the Pauli matrices and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ has basis $T_1,T_2,T_3$. Thus $[T_a,T_b]=\epsilon_{abc}T_c$ and $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g$ is dimensionless. The scalar field is one real adjoint Higgs field: a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued map $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^3$, viewed as the real form in the complexified adjoint representation. A gauge connection is a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form $A=A_i dx^i$. In a local section change $s_j=s_i h_{ij}$, use the right-action convention $A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+h_{ij}^{-1}dh_{ij}$ and $\Phi_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}\Phi_i$. Define

$$F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j],\qquad D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi],\qquad B_i=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}.$$

The static Prasad–Sommerfield sector has $\partial_tA_i=\partial_t\Phi=0$, $A_0=0$, no other dynamical fields, and identically zero Higgs potential. Its adopted energy functional is

$$E[A,\Phi]=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x.$$

The field dimensions are $[A_i]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and $[F_{ij}]=[B_i]=[D_i\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, so $E$ has dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$. A configuration is finite-energy when this integral is finite.

The boundary data fix a number $v>0$ of dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and require $|\Phi|_\kappa\to v$ and $n_\infty(\omega):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\Phi(R\omega)/v$ to exist smoothly on the unit sphere $S^2$ of spatial directions. Here $|X|_\kappa^2:=\kappa(X,X)$. The limiting tangential covariant derivative of $n_\infty$ vanishes, and the limiting magnetic field lies in the pointwise stabilizer Lie algebra $\{X\in\mathfrak{su}(2):[X,n_\infty(\omega)]=0\}$. The stabilizer subgroup of $T_3$ is $U(1)=\{\exp(\theta T_3):\theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. On closed northern and southern hemispheres choose smooth local lifts $u_N,u_S$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}T_3=n_\infty$; their equatorial transition is $u_S=u_N h$ with $h(\varphi)=\exp(\theta(\varphi)T_3)$, where $\varphi\in[0,2\pi]$ parametrizes the equator and $\theta:[0,2\pi]\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth lift. The local adapted frames, connection forms, and curvature forms extend smoothly, respectively $C^1$, to open neighborhoods of the closed hemispheres. The surface limit below exists. The admissible external Wilson probes include the fundamental doublet, on which $T_3$ has weights $\pm\tfrac12$; this specifies the electric probe lattice without adding a propagating fundamental matter field. Define the classical magnetic surface charge and its energy normalization by

$$m:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\,\hat x_i\,dS,\qquad T:=g^{-2}m,$$

where $\hat x=x/|x|$ is the outward unit normal and $dS$ is Euclidean area. The transition increment $\theta(2\pi)-\theta(0)$ is not assumed to be quantized in this definition. These are adopted classical model data; they assert no empirical law, quantum continuum construction, supersymmetry representation, or quantum BPS state.

Definition.text: Assume AC. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) and use the product Milnor model \(ET=(E_{S^1})^r\), \(BT=ET/T\), with right diagonal action \((e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)\). For \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), put \(A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\cong k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]\), where \(u_i=c_1(L_{\chi_i})\) is the degree-two class of the \(i\)th coordinate character line. For a smooth character \(\chi:T\to S^1\), set \(L_\chi=ET\times_T\mathbb C_\chi\), with the right equivalence \((e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)\). If \(\chi=\chi_{\mathbf n}\) for \(\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^r\), then \(c_1(L_\chi)=\sum_i n_i u_i\). Define \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) to consist of \(1\) and all finite products of \(c_1(L_\chi)\) for nontrivial characters \(\chi\). This is a multiplicative subset of \(A_T(k)\) with \(0\notin\mathscr S_T(k)\). For a topological space \(X\) with a continuous left \(T\)-action, set \(H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)\), with its \(A_T(k)\)-module structure induced by \(ET\times_T X\to BT\). For an \(A_T(k)\)-module \(N\), its localization \(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}N\) consists of fractions \(n/s\), with \(n\in N\), \(s\in\mathscr S_T(k)\), and \(n/s=n'/s'\) exactly when \(u(s'n-sn')=0\) for some \(u\in\mathscr S_T(k)\); addition is \((n/s)+(n'/s')=(s'n+sn')/(ss')\), and scalar multiplication is induced by the localized ring. The character-localized Borel equivariant cohomology is \(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(X;k)\). For \(r=0\), there are no nontrivial characters and \(\mathscr S_T(k)=\{1\}\).

Postulate.text:
Adopt independently a rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ pure Yang–Mills model on oriented and time-oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with increasing $x^0$ time orientation and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The global group is $SU(2)$, with one supplied smooth right principal bundle $P\to M$ and smooth equivariant local trivializations. The connection and its curvature are $A$ and $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, in the right-action convention of the Yang–Mills model supplier. Use anti-Hermitian $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$; let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be its complex-bilinear extension and $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$. Fix $g>0$ dimensionless and theta angle zero. A bundle sector means its smooth equivariant isomorphism class over $M$; only the supplied sector is used.

The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty. The vector multiplet comprises the connection, one complex adjoint scalar $\phi$, and two adjoint left-Weyl fermions. In $\mathcal N=1$ packaging it is a real adjoint vector superfield $V$ and an adjoint chiral superfield $\Phi$, not a matter hypermultiplet. Use the supplied superspace derivatives, chirality, ordered Berezin measures and vector-supergauge convention, including

$$\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^2(e^{-2gV_R}D_\alpha e^{2gV_R}),\qquad [X]_D=-\tfrac14 I_D(X),\qquad [Y]_F=\tfrac12 I_F(Y).$$

Here $\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}$ is the represented matrix curvature, not the abstract Lie-algebra curvature used in the action. With Hermitian $t_{a,R}=i\rho_{R*}(T_a)$, let $W_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a$ denote the canonically normalized component field-strength superfields, so $\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}=2g\,t_{a,R}W_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a$. Define the abstract connection-normalized curvature by

$$\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha}=gT_aW_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a,\qquad \rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})=\frac{\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}}{2i}.$$

In the fundamental representation, $\kappa_{\mathbb C}=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}$ therefore gives $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}^\alpha,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(\mathcal C^\alpha\mathcal C_\alpha)$, with the same ordered spinor product on both sides. This is a classical representation/component normalization, not a quantum field-rescaling or threshold-matching theorem.

Adopt the connection-normalized microscopic action

$$S_{\mathrm{pure}}=\int_M d^4x\left\{\frac1{g^2}[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi)]_D+\left(\left[\frac1{4g^2}\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}^\alpha,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})\right]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\}.$$

Here $I_D,I_F$ are the raw ordered mathematical integrals, and the physical action brackets and chiral components use [[def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization]]. The Hermitian-conjugate operation applies only to the chiral F term; the D term is real. Equivalently, the fundamental matrix F integrand is $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(\mathcal C^\alpha\mathcal C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$, plus its Hermitian conjugate. Its bosonic gauge density is fixed to $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g^2)$. There is no chiral superpotential, hypermultiplet, hypermultiplet mass, or FI parameter in this ultraviolet datum. The scalar is connection-normalized; its canonical version is $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$. In the same local Berezin normalization the quadratic microscopic prepotential is $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}(\Phi)=i\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi,\Phi)/(2g^2)$, with positive imaginary Hessian $\kappa/g^2$. The prepotential has mass dimension two. The dimensions are $[x]=-1$, $[\theta]=-1/2$, $[A]=[\phi]=1$, $[F_A]=2$, $[\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}]=[\mathcal C]=3/2$, and $[g]=0$.

Eight real rigid supercharges, their $\mathcal N=2$ algebra and invariance of this adopted action are model premises, not a locally proved invariance theorem. Variations are smooth and compactly supported; actions are on relatively compact regions or where integrable. A small $\mathcal N=1$ adjoint-mass perturbation and the Seiberg–Witten solution are separate subsequent inputs. In particular an emergent infrared monopole hypermultiplet is not microscopic matter added to this pure model. This postulate defines classical ultraviolet field/action data; it constructs no quantum measure, regulator limit, interacting continuum theory, or empirical verification.

Let $\mathscr R$ be the ring of even smooth chiral superfields on the specified flat superspace, with coefficients in the finite-dimensional supercommutative complex algebra of the superspace definition. Thus $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}f=0$ for $f\in\mathscr R$; its even elements commute. Fix an integer $n\geq1$, identify a specified based complex vector space $E$ with $\mathbb C^n$ and its dual with row vectors, and take $Q\in\mathscr R^n$, $\widetilde Q\in(\mathscr R^n)^*$ and $M\in M_n(\mathscr R)$. Suppose an invertible even chiral matrix $U\in GL_n(\mathscr R)$ acts by the explicitly supplied substitutions

$$Q'=UQ,\qquad \widetilde Q'=\widetilde Q U^{-1},\qquad M'=UMU^{-1}.$$

Then the chiral polynomials $\widetilde Q Q$ and $\widetilde Q M Q$ are invariant. In particular $\sqrt2\,\widetilde Q M Q+m\widetilde Q Q$ is invariant for every constant $m\in\mathbb C$. Assigning the formal degrees $[Q]=[\widetilde Q]=[M]=[m]=1$ makes this sum homogeneous of degree three. These are algebraic claims about the supplied action; they require no physical model or asserted supersymmetry realization. For the application $M=\rho_{R*}(\Phi)$, the same conclusion holds whenever that represented adjoint field has the stated conjugation law.

Definition.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{psmallmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{psmallmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Statement.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix an integer $n\ge1$, put
$P=\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]$, and let $\mathfrak m=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$.
Let $A_0=P_{\mathfrak m}$ be the localization at the polynomials nonzero at
the origin, let $H=\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$ be the ring of holomorphic
function germs at the origin, and let $T=\mathbb C\llbracket w_1,\ldots,w_n\rrbracket$ be the
formal power-series ring. For any finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq
\mathfrak m$, set $A_I=A_0/IA_0$ and $H_I=H/IH$. For a local ring $R$ with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, define its completion by
$\widehat R=\varprojlim_{k\ge1}R/\mathfrak m_R^k$.

The polynomial-to-germ map induces a local homomorphism $A_I\to H_I$. The
four rings $A_0,H,A_I,H_I$ are Noetherian local rings, and the induced map on
completions identifies both $\widehat{A_I}$ and $\widehat{H_I}$ canonically
with $T/IT$. In particular, the comparison uses the same extended defining
ideal $I$ and does not replace it by its radical, so nilpotent classes are
retained.

Statement.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbb C$
and let $x\in X$ be a closed point with residue field $\mathbb C$. Choose an
affine neighborhood of $x$ presented as (adding a dummy coordinate if needed)
$\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]/I)$, with $n\ge1$, $I$ a
finitely generated polynomial ideal contained in $(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$, and $x$
the origin. Write
$A=(\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]_{(w_1,\ldots,w_n)})/I\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]_{(w_1,\ldots,w_n)}$.
On this chart, define the analytic local ring by extending the same ideal to
holomorphic germs,
$B=\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}/I\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$; this quotient
retains the given scheme structure, including nilpotents. For a local ring $R$
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, let
$\widehat R=\varprojlim_{k\ge1}R/\mathfrak m_R^k$.

The canonical local homomorphism $A\to B$, which sends each polynomial class
to the same holomorphic germ, is injective and faithfully flat.
Its induced map $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is an isomorphism, with both
completions canonically identified with
$\mathbb C\llbracket w_1,\ldots,w_n\rrbracket/I\mathbb C\llbracket w_1,\ldots,w_n\rrbracket$. For every
$A$-module $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_A B$ is injective, and the quotient
$B/A$ is a flat $A$-module. These are local-ring conclusions; no relative
direct-image comparison is asserted.

Statement.text: Let $M$ be the coefficient-image subspace of a linear monad on $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ after removing its constant orthogonal summand as in the preceding splitting lemma. Thus its reduced middle cohomology has no global sections, is trivial on every $\sigma$-invariant real line, and has a positive section pairing on each such line. Let $H$ be the induced nondegenerate Hermitian form on $M$, linear in the first variable, and suppose $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and $\beta(z)\alpha(z)=0$ for every $z\in\mathbb C^4$, with $j^2=-1$. Then $H$ is positive definite on all of $M$.

Statement.text:
Assume AC and the exact rank-two regular zero-FI ADHM/ASD correspondence, with all its actual analytic and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites. Fix $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,1}$ be the orbit set by $U(V)$ of $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ with

$$[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad [B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0,$$

such that words in the $B_i$ applied to $I(W)$ span $V$ and no nonzero common invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$. On the positively stereographically oriented unit round $S^4$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,1}$ be the set of smooth Hermitian line bundles $L$, smooth unitary connections $A$ with $F_A^+=0$, and unitary framings $\Phi:L_\infty\to\mathbb C$, with $q_1=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int F_A\wedge F_A=-k$, modulo framed unitary isomorphisms. After a fixed framed bundle is chosen, its gauge group consists of smooth unitary automorphisms equal to identity at infinity.

The regular complex $GL(V)$ quotient, defined by retaining the complex equation and the same stability and costability, has the same empty-or-point classification under the zero-FI real/complex quotient identification. For $k>0$ both ordinary sets are empty. For $k=0$ they are the single empty raw datum and the framed flat line, respectively, with no framed stabilizer. This identification is equivariant for $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$, with $h=e^{-1}$, raw action $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$ and connection action by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing with $h$; on the resulting point these actions are trivial.

A first-order real Hermitian family here is over $D=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ with involution $\varepsilon^\dagger=\varepsilon$. On the raw side use free $D$-modules of ranks $k,1$, the displayed equations over $D$, regular reduction, fixed framing module, and unitary $D$-linear changes of basis. On the connection side use locally free smooth Hermitian line-bundle deformations with framed special fiber and a unitary connection $A_0+\varepsilon a$, satisfying ASD coefficientwise, modulo unitary gauge transformations with framed reduction and value identity at infinity. For $k>0$ these groupoids are empty; for $k=0$ each is equivalent to the one-object groupoid with trivial automorphism group. The identification commutes with reduction, infinitesimal scalar base changes preserving the involution, and the compact action. In particular it identifies their zero tangent spaces and restricts to the exact locally-free/base-change family range in the rank-two correspondence. No positive-FI quotient, its non-locally-free rank-one boundary, or its fixed-point series is identified with ordinary ASD moduli.

manifest_declaration.title: Rank-one regular zero-FI ADHM and ordinary ASD boundary
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume AC and the exact rank-two regular zero-FI ADHM/ASD correspondence, with all its actual analytic and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites. Fix $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,1}$ be the orbit set by $U(V)$ of $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ with

$$[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad [B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0,$$

such that words in the $B_i$ applied to $I(W)$ span $V$ and no nonzero common invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$. On the positively stereographically oriented unit round $S^4$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,1}$ be the set of smooth Hermitian line bundles $L$, smooth unitary connections $A$ with $F_A^+=0$, and unitary framings $\Phi:L_\infty\to\mathbb C$, with $q_1=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int F_A\wedge F_A=-k$, modulo framed unitary isomorphisms. After a fixed framed bundle is chosen, its gauge group consists of smooth unitary automorphisms equal to identity at infinity.

The regular complex $GL(V)$ quotient, defined by retaining the complex equation and the same stability and costability, has the same empty-or-point classification under the zero-FI real/complex quotient identification. For $k>0$ both ordinary sets are empty. For $k=0$ they are the single empty raw datum and the framed flat line, respectively, with no framed stabilizer. This identification is equivariant for $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$, with $h=e^{-1}$, raw action $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$ and connection action by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing with $h$; on the resulting point these actions are trivial.

A first-order real Hermitian family here is over $D=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ with involution $\varepsilon^\dagger=\varepsilon$. On the raw side use free $D$-modules of ranks $k,1$, the displayed equations over $D$, regular reduction, fixed framing module, and unitary $D$-linear changes of basis. On the connection side use locally free smooth Hermitian line-bundle deformations with framed special fiber and a unitary connection $A_0+\varepsilon a$, satisfying ASD coefficientwise, modulo unitary gauge transformations with framed reduction and value identity at infinity. For $k>0$ these groupoids are empty; for $k=0$ each is equivalent to the one-object groupoid with trivial automorphism group. The identification commutes with reduction, infinitesimal scalar base changes preserving the involution, and the compact action. In particular it identifies their zero tangent spaces and restricts to the exact locally-free/base-change family range in the rank-two correspondence. No positive-FI quotient, its non-locally-free rank-one boundary, or its fixed-point series is identified with ordinary ASD moduli.

Statement.text:
Assume full AC. Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ in algebraically independent variables. For $\chi=t_1^{m_1}t_2^{m_2}\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{n_\alpha}$ set $u_\chi=m_1\epsilon_1+m_2\epsilon_2+\sum_\alpha n_\alpha a_\alpha$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and
$$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

The quotient is a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite invariant affine word-slice atlas for the algebraic complex torus $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$. This result concerns the stable matrix quotient and a formal series. It asserts no sheaf/ASD dictionary or integration identity.

The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ in algebraically independent variables. For $\chi=t_1^{m_1}t_2^{m_2}\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{n_\alpha}$ set $u_\chi=m_1\epsilon_1+m_2\epsilon_2+\sum_\alpha n_\alpha a_\alpha$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and
$$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

The quotient is a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite invariant affine word-slice atlas for the algebraic complex torus $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$. This result concerns the stable matrix quotient and a formal series. It asserts no sheaf/ASD dictionary or integration identity.

Example.text: Assume full AC and take the explicit unit round spin $S^4$ background with $E=S^+$ and its positive-spin Levi-Civita connection, one massless left-handed Weyl doublet of a nondynamical $SU(2)$ global symmetry, and the order-two central transformation $z=-I$ specified in the global-anomaly test. The local Hodge calculation gives complex chiral index $1$ and Chern number $-1$; pair the boundary determinant/Pfaffian line with the five-dimensional bulk whose test-loop phase is $(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}_2D_5}$. The boundary line has character $\chi(1)=1$, $\chi(z)=-1$; the mapping-torus mod-two index is $1$, so the bulk character is $\chi^{-1}=\chi$ and the combined character is trivial. The local index-density anomaly polynomial is zero. For the finite normalization check take a single-vertex complex $K$ and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2$. The combined unit weight is arrow-invariant and its normalized groupoid sum is $1/2$. Without the bulk, the odd boundary character is not a scalar invariant weight and no such finite gauging sum is defined. For two identical copies the boundary character itself is trivial and the same normalized groupoid sum applies. This example tests only the stated loop and does not establish that even copies have no other anomalies.

Statement.text:
Fix $m>0$, $\Lambda>0$, integers $r\ge1$, $D\ge4$ and $N\ge1$, and the metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use the finite-jet operator quotient $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/R_D$ for one commuting scalar $\phi$ of weight one, field-degree cutoff four, derivative cutoff $r$, and complex orthogonal spacetime-index action preserving $\eta$. Let $U_D\subset V_D$ be the subspace of degree-exactly-four scalar polynomials whose indices are contracted using $\eta$ only, and let $Q_D^{(4)}$ be its image in $\mathcal Q_D$. Thus $Q_D^{(4)}=U_D/(U_D\cap R_D)$; operators outside this image are not assigned a contact map.

Require the following certificate for the actual declared relations: every $H\in U_D\cap R_D$ is a finite sum of identically zero jet polynomials, total divergences $\partial_\mu J^\mu$ with $J$ quartic, and $F(\Box-m^2)\phi$ with $F$ cubic, where $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$. The summands may use a larger finite jet space and different engineering weights; their polynomial sum must equal $H$ before any on-shell substitution. This is an additional restriction on the selected $R_D$, not a claim about an arbitrary relation subspace or its completeness.

For $O\in U_D$ introduce commuting indeterminates $z_1,\ldots,z_4$ and complex four-vectors $k_1,\ldots,k_4$. Its polarized Fourier vertex is

$$T_O(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=[z_1z_2z_3z_4]\,O\!\left(\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_a}\phi\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^4 z_j i^a k_{j,\mu_1}\cdots k_{j,\mu_a}\right).$$

The coefficient convention contains no $1/4!$. Impose $\sum_jk_j=0$, $k_j^2=-m^2$, and set $s=-(k_1+k_2)^2$, $t=-(k_1+k_3)^2$, $u=-(k_1+k_4)^2$. Replace contracted products by $k_j^2=-m^2$, $k_1\cdot k_2=k_3\cdot k_4=m^2-s/2$, $k_1\cdot k_3=k_2\cdot k_4=m^2-t/2$, and $k_1\cdot k_4=k_2\cdot k_3=m^2-u/2$. Put $t=0$, $s=2m^2+v$, $u=2m^2-v$, obtaining a polynomial $t_O(v)$. Define $\nu_0=2m^2$ and the linear contact-jet map

$$M_{D,N}([O])_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}\Lambda^{4-D}[v^{2k+2}]t_O(v),\qquad 0\le k\le N.$$

Then this map $Q_D^{(4)}\to\mathbb C^{N+1}$ is well-defined, $t_O$ is even, and it takes real operator classes to real vectors. For $D=8$, $O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ satisfies

$$t_{O_8}(v)=8m^4+4v^2,\qquad M_{8,N}([C_8O_8])=(4\nu_0^2C_8/\Lambda^4,0,\ldots,0).$$

In particular the coefficient $[v^2]\Lambda^{-4}t_{C_8O_8}=4C_8/\Lambda^4$ is invariant under the certified relations. The target has precisely the normalized coordinate convention of the finite forward-amplitude problem. This algebraic map describes one quartic contact insertion about the free massive scalar quadratic action. It does not equate the contact polynomial to an exact full amplitude, discard loop or other-operator contributions, or infer positivity of a perturbative term from positivity of a full amplitude.

Example.text:
Let $G=\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo $2$, and define $\omega:G^3\to\mathbb C^\times$ by $\omega(a,b,c)=(-1)^{abc}$. Let $\operatorname{Vec}_{G}^{\omega}$ have as objects finite-dimensional complex $G$-graded vector spaces, as morphisms grade-preserving linear maps, tensor product
$$(W\otimes U)_c=\bigoplus_{a+b=c}W_a\otimes_{\mathbb C}U_b,$$
and unit $\delta_0$, the one-dimensional line in grade $0$. Write $\delta_a$ for the one-dimensional line in grade $a$. On homogeneous lines take the associator
$$\alpha_{\delta_a,\delta_b,\delta_c}=\omega(a,b,c)\operatorname{id}_{\delta_{a+b+c}},$$
and extend it linearly to direct sums. Since $\omega$ is a normalized $3$-cocycle, this defines a finite semisimple fusion category with $\delta_a\otimes\delta_b\cong\delta_{a+b}$. In particular, $\delta_1\otimes\delta_1\cong\delta_0$, while $\alpha_{\delta_1,\delta_1,\delta_1}=-\operatorname{id}_{\delta_1}$. The untwisted choice $\omega\equiv1$ has the same fusion multiplicities but associator $+\operatorname{id}_{\delta_1}$ on that triple. Thus the fusion multiplicities alone do not record the specified associator component; no claim about monoidal inequivalence of these two categories is made.

Example.text:
Let $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ have metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $\phi:M\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth compactly supported real scalar field of engineering dimension one. Let $m\geq0$ and $\Lambda>0$ have mass dimension one, let $g,C\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless, and let $\epsilon$ be a dimensionless formal parameter with $\epsilon^2=0$. For dimension bookkeeping, adjoin a central formal scalar $M_s$ of engineering weight one and specialize $M_s=m$ only after forming homogeneous expressions. Let $\widehat W_6$ be the finite complex vector space of polynomials of weight six in $M_s$ and the scalar field jets, with derivative cutoff two and field-degree cutoff six; take the symmetry group to be trivial. Let $\widehat R_6$ be spanned by its total divergences and the density $\phi^3\widehat{\mathcal E}_0$, where $\widehat{\mathcal E}_0=\Box\phi-M_s^2\phi-(g/6)\phi^3$, and write $\widehat{\mathcal Q}_6=\widehat W_6/\widehat R_6$. For compactly supported densities define $\mathcal I[f]=\int_M f\,d^4x$ and impose $\mathcal I(\partial_\mu J^\mu)=0$ for every compactly supported current. Write $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ and set

$$
S_0[\phi]=\mathcal I\!\left[-\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-\frac12m^2\phi^2-\frac{g}{4!}\phi^4\right],\qquad \mathcal O_6=\phi^2\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi,
$$

with $S_\epsilon=S_0+\epsilon(C/\Lambda^2)\mathcal I(\mathcal O_6)$. After specializing $M_s=m$, the leading Euler derivative is $\mathcal E_0=\Box\phi-m^2\phi-(g/6)\phi^3$. In $\widehat{\mathcal Q}_6$,

$$
[\mathcal O_6]= -\frac{1}{3}[M_s^2\phi^4]-\frac{g}{18}[\phi^6].
$$

The identity-leading local change of variables $\phi\mapsto\phi+\epsilon C\phi^3/(3\Lambda^2)$ transforms the action through this order to

$$
S_\epsilon\!\left[\phi+\epsilon\frac{C\phi^3}{3\Lambda^2}\right] = S_0[\phi]-\epsilon\frac{Cm^2}{3\Lambda^2}\mathcal I(\phi^4)-\epsilon\frac{Cg}{18\Lambda^2}\mathcal I(\phi^6).
$$

The mass spurion gives each term in the quotient identity weight six. Give the formal coefficient $\Lambda^{-1}$ weight $-1$; multiplying the identity by $C/\Lambda^2$ then places every term in a finite weight-four action-density space, and $F[\phi]\mathcal E_0$ lies in that space for $F[\phi]=-C\phi^3/(3\Lambda^2)$. Example.text:
Let $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ have metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $\phi:M\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth compactly supported real scalar field of engineering dimension one. Let $m\geq0$ and $\Lambda>0$ have mass dimension one, let $g,C\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless, and let $\epsilon$ be a dimensionless formal parameter with $\epsilon^2=0$. For dimension bookkeeping, adjoin a central formal scalar $M_s$ of engineering weight one and specialize $M_s=m$ only after forming homogeneous expressions. Let $\widehat W_6$ be the finite complex vector space of polynomials of weight six in $M_s$ and the scalar field jets, with derivative cutoff two and field-degree cutoff six; take the symmetry group to be trivial. Let $\widehat R_6$ be spanned by its total divergences and the density $\phi^3\widehat{\mathcal E}_0$, where $\widehat{\mathcal E}_0=\Box\phi-M_s^2\phi-(g/6)\phi^3$, and write $\widehat{\mathcal Q}_6=\widehat W_6/\widehat R_6$. For compactly supported densities define $\mathcal I[f]=\int_M f\,d^4x$ and impose $\mathcal I(\partial_\mu J^\mu)=0$ for every compactly supported current. Write $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ and set

$$
S_0[\phi]=\mathcal I\!\left[-\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-\frac12m^2\phi^2-\frac{g}{4!}\phi^4\right],\qquad \mathcal O_6=\phi^2\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi,
$$

with $S_\epsilon=S_0+\epsilon(C/\Lambda^2)\mathcal I(\mathcal O_6)$. After specializing $M_s=m$, the leading Euler derivative is $\mathcal E_0=\Box\phi-m^2\phi-(g/6)\phi^3$. In $\widehat{\mathcal Q}_6$,

$$
[\mathcal O_6]= -\frac{1}{3}[M_s^2\phi^4]-\frac{g}{18}[\phi^6].
$$

The identity-leading local change of variables $\phi\mapsto\phi+\epsilon C\phi^3/(3\Lambda^2)$ transforms the action through this order to

$$
S_\epsilon\!\left[\phi+\epsilon\frac{C\phi^3}{3\Lambda^2}\right] = S_0[\phi]-\epsilon\frac{Cm^2}{3\Lambda^2}\mathcal I(\phi^4)-\epsilon\frac{Cg}{18\Lambda^2}\mathcal I(\phi^6).
$$

The mass spurion gives each term in the quotient identity weight six. Give the formal coefficient $\Lambda^{-1}$ weight $-1$; multiplying the identity by $C/\Lambda^2$ then places every term in a finite weight-four action-density space, and $F[\phi]\mathcal E_0$ lies in that space for $F[\phi]=-C\phi^3/(3\Lambda^2)$. The map uses the convention $\Psi(\phi)=\phi-\epsilon F[\phi]$, and $\epsilon F$ has the units of $\phi$. This is a formal scalar-action calculation under the stated boundary convention; it asserts neither a physical realization nor an on-shell scattering result.

Statement.text:
Let $v>0$, let $J=(-v,\infty)$, and use the linearly transforming complex doublet $H$ with hypercharge $Y=1/2$ and the nonlinear fields $h\in J$, $U\in SU(2)$, with the gauge transformations and mostly-plus Minkowski conventions of the two adopted electroweak models. Here $\sigma^2=\begin{psmallmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{psmallmatrix}$ is the second Pauli matrix. Put $e_2=(0,1)^T$, $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$, and define
$$\Phi:J\times SU(2)\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\},\qquad \Phi(h,U)=\frac{v+h}{\sqrt2}Ue_2.$$
Then $\Phi$ is a smooth diffeomorphism onto the nonzero-doublet field space. Its inverse is obtained from $\rho=(H^\dagger H)^{1/2}>0$ and $\Sigma(H)=(\widetilde H,H)$ by
$$h=\sqrt2\rho-v,\qquad U=\frac{\Sigma(H)}{\rho}.$$
It is equivariant for $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$: for $g_L\in SU(2)_L$ and $z\in U(1)_Y$, under $H\mapsto g_Lz^3H$ one has $U\mapsto g_LU\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3})^{-1}$ and $h\mapsto h$. The point $H=0$ is excluded; no value of $U$ is assigned there.

For the finite selected SMEFT interaction consisting of the renormalizable terms and the source-defined Warsaw representatives through canonical dimension six, substitute $H=\Phi(h,U)$ and its conjugate into each representative and expand covariant derivatives by the product rule. In the unnormalized radial variable $x=h/v$, every resulting coefficient function multiplying a fixed finite HEFT derivative/Goldstone monomial is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most six. More precisely, after choosing a finite ordered list of the resulting HEFT monomials and a common dimensionally consistent coefficient normalization, the HEFT coefficient tuple is $f=R c$, where $c$ is the finite selected SMEFT coefficient tuple and $R$ is the finite matrix defined by this substitution. Thus its functions and coefficients obey the polynomial and linear-image correlations of this selected branch; they are not freely specifiable smooth HEFT functions. For example, an independent coefficient function $e^x$ is not in the degree-at-most-six polynomial class on any open interval. These radial functions are analytic in $h/v$ before any further field reparametrization.

The canonical-dimension cutoff and the separately defined HEFT chiral/loop grading remain distinct: the substitution does not identify all HEFT classes through a chosen chiral order with the Warsaw list. The result is a conditional statement about the named finite coefficient representatives and their local field substitution, not a proof that a formal algebraic invariant quotient equals the full physical compact-gauge invariant space. It asserts neither that every HEFT lies on this branch nor that every HEFT point has a weakly coupled ultraviolet completion.
