Example.text:
Use the selected mostly-plus, four-dimensional electroweak model with $v>0$, dimensionless gauge coupling $g>0$, and coefficient scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$. Choose a real dimensionless coefficient $C_{H\Box}$, set all other dimension-six coefficients to zero, and retain
$$Q_{H\Box}=(H^\dagger H)\Box(H^\dagger H),\qquad \Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu,$$
with Lagrangian contribution $C_{H\Box}Q_{H\Box}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2$. On the nonzero-doublet patch use the local unitary-gauge field configuration $U=I$ and $H=(0,(v+h)/\sqrt2)^T$. Impose compact support or boundary conditions that make the surface term in the action vanish.

The quadratic scalar coefficient after integration by parts is
$$K(h)=1+\frac{2C_{H\Box}(v+h)^2}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}.$$
If
$$K(0)=1+\frac{2C_{H\Box}v^2}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}>0,$$
then $K$ is positive on some open interval about $h=0$. In that interval define the locally canonical radial coordinate $\widehat h(h)=\int_0^h\sqrt{K(s)}\,ds$. Define $W_\mu^\pm=(W_\mu^1\mp iW_\mu^2)/\sqrt2$ and define $m_W^2(h)$ as the coefficient in the vector mass term $-m_W^2(h)W_\mu^+W^{-\mu}$. The charged-vector mass parameter and its dimensionless linear coupling in this coordinate are
$$m_W^2(h)=\frac{g^2(v+h)^2}{4},\qquad \kappa_W:=\left.\frac{v}{2m_W^2(0)}\frac{dm_W^2}{d\widehat h}\right|_{h=0}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2C_{H\Box}v^2/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}}.$$
These are conditional tree-level coefficient predictions of this selected local action. Interpret $h=0$ as a vacuum only when the supplied total scalar potential has the local minimum required by the SMEFT model; otherwise these are coefficients at the reference configuration. No measured value, coefficient fit, loop correction, discarded-order bound, or general HEFT relation is asserted.

Statement.text:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth manifold of finite dimension $n$, with integration cycle $M$, smooth positive volume form $\mu$, graded algebra $\mathcal A=\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)$, and integral $I_\Gamma(F)=\int_M F_{[n]}$ of the degree-$n$ part. Let $Q$ be a smooth odd derivation of $\mathcal A$, let $S,O$ be smooth even forms, let $V$ be a smooth odd form, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval. Suppose $QS=QO=0$, $(Q^2V)e^{-S-tQV}=0$ for every $t\in J$, and $I_\Gamma(Q(O V e^{-S-tQV}))=0$ for every $t\in J$, including the zero-boundary-flux condition. Write $(Oe^{-S-tQV})_{[n]}=f_t\mu$. Suppose that $f_t$ is integrable for each $t\in J$, is differentiable in $t$ almost everywhere with measurable derivative, and that for every compact $K\subset J$ one integrable majorant $g_K$ bounds both $|f_t|$ and $|\partial_t f_t|$ for all $t\in K$, outside one null set. Then

$$Z(t):=I_\Gamma(Oe^{-S-tQV})=\int_M f_t\,d\mu$$

is constant on $J$, and for every $t\in J$,

$$Z'(t)=-I_\Gamma(O(QV)e^{-S-tQV})=-I_\Gamma(Q(O V e^{-S-tQV}))=0.$$

In particular, the conclusion is finite-dimensional and applies only at finite parameter values in $J$; it gives no $t\to\infty$ saddle-point limit and no identity for an infinite-dimensional continuum functional integral.

Example.text: Let $\Gamma$ be the finite oriented boundary cycle of a square, with four edges $e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4$ and one plaquette. Use the compact matrix group $G=SU(2)=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-\overline b&\overline a\end{pmatrix}:a,b\in\mathbb C,\ |a|^2+|b|^2=1\right\}$ in its defining two-dimensional representation. Assign one link variable $U_j\in G$ to each edge and set the ordered plaquette holonomy to $U_p=U_1U_2U_3^{-1}U_4^{-1}$. The group is the unit sphere $S^3$ in the $(a,b)$ coordinates; let $\mu$ be its normalized round surface measure. For $\beta\ge0$, define the dimensionless action $S_\beta(U)=\beta\left(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}U_p\right)$ and partition function $Z_\beta=\int_{G^4}e^{-S_\beta(U)}\,d\mu^{\otimes4}(U)$. This finite graph integral satisfies $e^{-2\beta}\le Z_\beta\le1$, so it is finite and strictly positive. It has only four group variables and defines no continuum fields, no Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction, and no Hamiltonian; it therefore does not solve the four-dimensional existence and mass-gap problem.

Example.text: Let $\Gamma$ be the finite oriented boundary cycle of a square, with four edges $e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4$ and one plaquette. Use the compact matrix group $G=SU(2)=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-\overline b&\overline a\end{pmatrix}:a,b\in\mathbb C,\ |a|^2+|b|^2=1\right\}$ in its defining two-dimensional representation. Assign one link variable $U_j\in G$ to each edge and set the ordered plaquette holonomy to $U_p=U_1U_2U_3^{-1}U_4^{-1}$. The group is the unit sphere $S^3$ in the $(a,b)$ coordinates; let $\mu$ be its normalized round surface measure. For $\beta\ge0$, define the dimensionless action $S_\beta(U)=\beta\left(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}U_p\right)$ and partition function $Z_\beta=\int_{G^4}e^{-S_\beta(U)}\,d\mu^{\otimes4}(U)$. This finite graph integral satisfies $e^{-2\beta}\le Z_\beta\le1$, so it is finite and strictly positive. It has only four group variables and defines no continuum fields, no Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction, and no Hamiltonian; it therefore does not solve the four-dimensional existence and mass-gap problem.

Example.text: Let $\mathbb{H}$ be the real quaternion algebra with basis $1,i,j,k$, multiplication $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$, and norm $|a+bi+cj+dk|^2=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2$. A Lie group is a finite-dimensional smooth manifold with smooth multiplication and inversion; its Lie algebra is its tangent space at the identity with the bracket induced by left-invariant vector fields. Let $SU(2)$ be the group of unit quaternions and $SO(3)$ the group of linear maps of $\operatorname{Im}\mathbb{H}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k\}\cong\mathbb R^3$ preserving the Euclidean inner product and having determinant $+1$. A Lie algebra is simple if it is nonabelian and has no nonzero proper ideals. For this example, a compact simple gauge group means a compact connected Lie group with a simple Lie algebra. Its global form means the Lie group itself, including its central quotient, rather than only its Lie algebra. The kernel of a group homomorphism is the inverse image of the identity, and the center is the set of elements commuting with every group element. The map $\pi:SU(2)\to SO(3)$ defined by $\pi(q)x=qxq^{-1}$ is a surjective homomorphism with kernel $\{1,-1\}$; its differential identifies the simple Lie algebras of $SU(2)$ and $SO(3)$, while the groups are distinct. Therefore, a proof of a claim quantified over every compact simple gauge group at $SU(2)$ alone does not discharge the separate $SO(3)$ case.

flat and induces the common completion $\mathbb C\llbracket t\rrbracket$, but it is not
surjective: the convergent exponential germ
$e(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t^n/n!$ is not in its image.

Example.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb C[x,y]/(x^2))$
and let $p$ be the closed $\mathbb C$-point at the origin. Its algebraic local
ring is $A=(\mathbb C[x,y]/(x^2))_{(x,y)}$, and its analytic local ring is
$B=\mathbb C\{x,y\}/(x^2)$. The canonical map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat
with common maximal-ideal completion $\mathbb C\llbracket x,y\rrbracket/(x^2)$, and the class
of $x$ is a nonzero element whose square is zero in both rings.

Statement.text:
Let $V=W=\mathbb C$, let $k=N=1$, and consider scalar ADHM data $(b_1,b_2,i,j)\in\mathbb C^4$ satisfying $ij=0$ and the stability condition $i\ne0$. Let $GL(V)=\mathbb C^\times$ act by $(b_1,b_2,i,j)\mapsto(b_1,b_2,\lambda i,\lambda^{-1}j)$, and let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times\mathbb C^\times_h$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(b_1,b_2,i,j)=(t_1b_1,t_2b_2,h^{-1}i,t_1t_2h j)$. Write $X$ for the geometric quotient of the stable locus. Extend $T$ by a flavor torus $\mathbb C_m^\times$ acting trivially on $X$, with additive character $\widetilde m$. The quotient is isomorphic to $\mathbb C^2$ with coordinates $b_1,b_2$, the fixed locus is the origin, and the tangent weights there are $\epsilon_1=c_1(t_1)$ and $\epsilon_2=c_1(t_2)$. If the localized Borel–Moore pushforward of the complex-oriented fundamental class with insertion $c_2^{T_m}(TX\otimes L_{-1})$ is defined, where $L_{-1}$ is the inverse flavor line of weight $-\widetilde m$, then the charge-one coefficient is
$$I_{1,1}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=\frac{(\epsilon_1-\widetilde m)(\epsilon_2-\widetilde m)}{\epsilon_1\epsilon_2}.$$

Statement.text:
Let $V=W=\mathbb C$, let $k=N=1$, and consider scalar ADHM data $(b_1,b_2,i,j)\in\mathbb C^4$ satisfying $ij=0$ and the stability condition $i\ne0$. Let $GL(V)=\mathbb C^\times$ act by $(b_1,b_2,i,j)\mapsto(b_1,b_2,\lambda i,\lambda^{-1}j)$, and let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times\mathbb C^\times_h$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(b_1,b_2,i,j)=(t_1b_1,t_2b_2,h^{-1}i,t_1t_2h j)$. Write $X$ for the geometric quotient of the stable locus. Extend $T$ by a flavor torus $\mathbb C_m^\times$ acting trivially on $X$, with additive character $\widetilde m$. The quotient is isomorphic to $\mathbb C^2$ with coordinates $b_1,b_2$, the fixed locus is the origin, and the tangent weights there are $\epsilon_1=c_1(t_1)$ and $\epsilon_2=c_1(t_2)$. If the localized Borel–Moore pushforward of the complex-oriented fundamental class with insertion $c_2^{T_m}(TX\otimes L_{-1})$ is defined, where $L_{-1}$ is the inverse flavor line of weight $-\widetilde m$, then the charge-one coefficient is
$$I_{1,1}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=\frac{(\epsilon_1-\widetilde m)(\epsilon_2-\widetilde m)}{\epsilon_1\epsilon_2}.$$
At charge zero the quotient is a point with rank-zero insertion and coefficient $1$.

Observations.text: The collaboration reports no significant excess over the Standard Model prediction in either search; all signal-region deviations are below 2 standard deviations. The observed displaced-track exclusion reaches about $m(\tilde\chi^\pm_1)=200$ GeV at $\Delta m=0.6$ GeV, and the one-lepton-plus-one-track exclusion reaches $m(\tilde\chi^\pm_1)=130$ GeV at $\Delta m=2$ GeV. Combining the searches, ATLAS reports exclusion of chargino masses below 126 GeV at 95% confidence level for $\Delta m$ from 0.3 to 2 GeV in the stated simplified higgsino model. These are collaboration-reported statistical inferences conditional on the analysis and model.

Observations.text: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the Standard Model and quotes a $99\%$ compatibility $p$-value for its specified goodness-of-fit test. It also identifies an electroweak-precision coefficient direction, denoted $c^{[19]}_{HVV,Vff}$ in the article, as pulled by the known tension between the measured $A_{\rm FB}^{b,c}$ asymmetries and the Standard Model prediction. The overall fit statement therefore does not mean that every coefficient is individually within two standard deviations. A $p$-value is a tail probability under the stated null calibration, not the probability that the Standard Model is true.

Observations.text: The collaboration reports that data are consistent with Standard Model expectations and that no significant deviations were observed. It reports the following observed mass reaches in the stated simplified models: gluino masses up to 2.25 TeV in T5ttcc, 2.35 TeV in T5qqqqWH, and 2.30 TeV in T5bbbbZH; top-squark masses up to 1.45 TeV in T6ttZH; nearly mass-degenerate chargino/neutralino masses up to 1.05 TeV in TChiWZ and 0.94 TeV in TChiWW; bottom-squark masses up to 0.97 TeV in R2bbqqlv; and gluino masses up to 1.82 TeV in R5ttbl. These values are 95% confidence-level limits as reported by CMS, and depend on each model's decay topology and other assumptions.

Open problem.text: For every compact connected finite-dimensional Lie group $G$ whose Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is nonabelian and has no nonzero proper Lie ideals, construct a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory with gauge group $G$. A Lie group is a smooth manifold with smooth multiplication and inversion, and its Lie algebra is its tangent space at the identity with the bracket induced by left-invariant vector fields. A Wightman realization means a theory satisfying the Wightman axioms: it supplies a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a unitary representation of translations and proper, orthochronous Lorentz isometries of Minkowski space $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$, and local quantum fields as operator-valued tempered distributions on Schwartz test functions acting on a common dense invariant domain. The fields transform covariantly; gauge-invariant fields localized in regions whose points are spacelike separated, meaning $\eta(x-y,x-y)>0$, commute. Correlation functions are the vacuum expectation distributions of finite products of smeared fields. The self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H$ generating time translations has spectrum $\sigma(H)\subseteq[0,\infty)$, and there is a unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum vector $\Omega$ up to phase with $H\Omega=0$. Alternatively, a Euclidean construction gives Schwinger distributions, meaning Euclidean vacuum correlation distributions on $\mathbb R^4$, satisfying the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms (temperedness, Euclidean covariance, reflection positivity, permutation symmetry, and clustering) strongly enough for reconstruction of a Wightman theory. The required nontrivial gauge content includes local operator fields corresponding to gauge-invariant local polynomials in a smooth connection's curvature and its covariant derivatives, with short-distance correlations prescribed in a specified construction by asymptotic freedom (the perturbative prediction that the gauge coupling tends to zero at short distances) and perturbative renormalization. It includes a local stress-energy tensor whose charges generate spacetime translations and an operator product expansion, meaning a short-distance expansion of products of local fields in local fields. Here the curvature of a smooth local connection $A$ is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, and its covariant derivative on adjoint-valued forms is $D_A=d+[A,\cdot]$. The required mass gap is a finite number $\Delta>0$ such that $\sigma(H)\cap(0,\Delta)=\varnothing$, using units $c=\hbar=1$. Confinement is a separate question and is not part of this problem.

A Lie group is a smooth manifold with smooth multiplication and inversion, and its Lie algebra is its tangent space at the identity with the bracket induced by left-invariant vector fields. A Wightman realization means a theory satisfying the Wightman axioms: it supplies a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a unitary representation of translations and proper, orthochronous Lorentz isometries of Minkowski space $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$, and local quantum fields as operator-valued tempered distributions on Schwartz test functions acting on a common dense invariant domain. The fields transform covariantly; gauge-invariant fields localized in regions whose points are spacelike separated, meaning $\eta(x-y,x-y)>0$, commute. Correlation functions are the vacuum expectation distributions of finite products of smeared fields. The self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H$ generating time translations has spectrum $\sigma(H)\subseteq[0,\infty)$, and there is a unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum vector $\Omega$ up to phase with $H\Omega=0$. Alternatively, a Euclidean construction gives Schwinger distributions, meaning Euclidean vacuum correlation distributions on $\mathbb R^4$, satisfying the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms (temperedness, Euclidean covariance, reflection positivity, permutation symmetry, and clustering) strongly enough for reconstruction of a Wightman theory. The required nontrivial gauge content includes local operator fields corresponding to gauge-invariant local polynomials in a smooth connection's curvature and its covariant derivatives, with short-distance correlations prescribed in a specified construction by asymptotic freedom (the perturbative prediction that the gauge coupling tends to zero at short distances) and perturbative renormalization. It includes a local stress-energy tensor whose charges generate spacetime translations and an operator product expansion, meaning a short-distance expansion of products of local fields in local fields. Here the curvature of a smooth local connection $A$ is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, and its covariant derivative on adjoint-valued forms is $D_A=d+[A,\cdot]$. The required mass gap is a finite number $\Delta>0$ such that $\sigma(H)\cap(0,\Delta)=\varnothing$, using units $c=\hbar=1$. Confinement is a separate question and is not part of this problem.

Statement.text:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Use the constant-metric connection-normalized dual model, explicitly in the linear truncation $u(A_D)=u_m+cA_D$, with $c\ne0$, $\mu\ne0$ and $g=g_D>0$. Put $v^2=|\mu c|/\sqrt2$, $\xi=2v^2$ and $e^{i\beta}=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v^2)$. Define charge-one fields

$$q=\frac{M+e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M}}{\sqrt2},\qquad p=\frac{M-e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M}}{\sqrt2},\qquad s=|q|^2+|p|^2.$$

Let $A=\widetilde A_1dx^1+\widetilde A_2dx^2$ be smooth and real on $\mathbb R^2$, $D_i=\partial_i-iA_i$, $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$ and $a=A_D$. For every smooth finite-energy profile in the uniform-vacuum winding-$n$ class, $n\ne0$, with $|q|\to\sqrt\xi$, $p,a\to0$ and limiting flux $2\pi n$, the positive-winding identity is

$$E=2\pi\xi n+\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{[B-g^2(\xi-s)]^2}{2g^2}+|(D_1+iD_2)q|^2+|(D_1+iD_2)p|^2+2g^2\xi|p|^2+g^{-2}|\partial_i a|^2+2|a|^2s\right\}d^2x.$$

The boundary current is removed along a radii subsequence furnished by finite energy and uniform bounded vacuum amplitudes; no full-circle current limit or extra exponential decay assumption is required. For negative winding conjugate the charged fields and reverse A, giving $E\ge2\pi\xi|n|=4\pi v^2|n|$.

For **every** nonzero integer n and every effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$, at arbitrary centres with arbitrary positive multiplicities, the actual planar vortex theorem supplies a smooth critical pair at $e=g$, with $(D_1+iD_2)q=0$, $B=g^2(\xi-|q|^2)$ for $n>0$ and the conjugate equations for $n<0$. Its embedding

$$a=p=0,\qquad M=q/\sqrt2,\qquad \widetilde M=e^{i\beta}\bar q/\sqrt2$$

is a stationary absolute transverse energy minimum among all the above full-model profiles with the same winding, with tension $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. This is actual existence and minimum energy, not an assumed solution. Gauge-invariant curvature and covariant gradients decay exponentially. Only the degree-zero correction relative to $n\theta$ is removed by a globally smooth gauge to obtain canonical exterior fields; the degree-changing local unwound gauge is not extended across the divisor.

For the precise classical cylinder problem, use the fixed-flux class $\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)$ of [[def-qftx-n2-nonlinear-magnetostatic-flux-cylinder]], specialized to this **linear** u and constant $b=g^{-2}$, with any fixed smooth canonical end profiles in one closed valid neutral disk and constant or omitted theta. For every chosen arbitrary-divisor minimizing profile above, actual smooth fixed-width finite-energy collars from both ends exist and give constants $\ell>0$, $C_0,C_1<\infty$ independent of L such that

$$T_nL\le I_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1\le T_nL+C_0+C_1\qquad(L\ge2\ell).$$

Thus $I_L=T_nL+O(1)$. Matching minimizing end traces give an exact translation-invariant minimum $T_nL$. The same estimate holds for any other stated fixed-flux boundary class which admits such collars; no unspecified probe-to-end-trace dictionary is inferred. In the special case $a=p=0$ at both ends, the mathematical critical cylinder theorem supplies the embedded collar construction directly. General full-model end profiles use the proved local magnetostatic collar construction, not an assumed endcap bound.

In linear response about the Higgs vacuum, original magnetic probes are dual electric sources for a vector of mass $m_D^2=2g^2\xi$; its unit canonical static source potential is $e^{-m_Dr}/(4\pi r)$, so that response is screened. The tube carries dual magnetic, hence original electric, flux in the adopted frame. These are classical boundary-energy statements, not a quantum Wilson-loop area law or an ultraviolet matching theorem.

For a generic nonlinear u, the same embedded fields with a=0 instead have the pointwise neutral potential derivative

$$\left.\partial_{\bar a}V_\mu\right|_{a=0}=g^2\bar\mu\,\overline{u''(0)}\bigl(\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu c\bigr).$$

If nonzero anywhere, the embedded profile is not stationary for that nonlinear model. The generic nonlinear theorem proves a positive limiting energy slope; it does not inherit exact critical BPS saturation or an $O(1)$ remainder from this theorem.
